requirements.requirement: Repair bin/upgrade.py so the v1-to-v2 migration preserves existing product IDs and descriptions and adds price_cents as a nonnegative field initialized to zero.
requirements.summary: The repaired script adds price_cents as INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a nonnegative CHECK. The live upgraded database retained products 1/Paper and 2/Tape with zero prices, rejected a negative price, and passed integrity checking.

requirements.requirement: Advance schema_version only after the entire upgrade succeeds, and leave the v1 database usable if an upgrade fails.
requirements.summary: The implementation performs the schema change, validation, and version update in one explicit transaction, with the version update last. An injected failure at that final update rolled back the added column, retained schema version 1 and the original rows, and left integrity_check successful.

requirements.requirement: Make the schema upgrade safe to repeat.
requirements.summary: Two consecutive executions succeeded on an isolated v1 database and two on the live database, leaving one valid price_cents column, schema version 2, intact data, and successful integrity checks. It also ran successfully again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic before and after execution and restart. The solution used the platform-provided Python 3 and SQLite and introduced no package changes.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, restart was acknowledged, the connection interruption was observed, the boot identity changed, and the system, executor agent, migration file, database integrity, schema, and product data recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots provide only bounded inventories and do not independently hash the task directory after execution; final task-file and database state therefore relies primarily on the direct executor observations.
There is no separate application service or cluster for this SQLite catalog; restart recovery evidence appropriately covers the single node, execution agent, migration file, and database state.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the repaired migration was task-required (cmd-b71bf67f09444d7f); isolated failure and repetition fixtures were bounded and removed by a trap (cmd-9e64b9c83cd14c81); the live database upgrade and rolled-back constraint probe directly verified required behavior (cmd-adcd842b6e1a4f61); and the reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol (cmd-17d7e30fd8e64d0a). Post-execution observations show no failed services, healthy package state, no task-created temporary residue, and no material new exposure. The apparent socket differences are PID/format changes and a normal DHCP socket following reboot.
